extracted.intended_audience: HHS/CMS policymakers and staff; healthcare providers and industry stakeholders (hospitals, physicians, nurses, therapists, pharmacies, medical device/lab stakeholders)
extracted.subtask_description: Advocacy comments responding to an HHS/CMS Request for Information proposing deregulatory changes across multiple healthcare sectors (home health, hospitals, physicians, nursing, pharmacy, medical devices/labs). Contains specific recommended regulatory amendments and justifications. Intended to guide agency rulemaking and regulatory review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allow therapists to perform initial and comprehensive assessments
rubrics_metrics.description: CMS should allow therapists to perform initial and comprehensive assessments in all therapy cases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: During the COVID-19 PHE, CMS waived §484.55(a)(2) and §484.55(b)(3) to allow rehabilitation skilled professionals to perform initial/comprehensive assessments when only therapy services were ordered. Stakeholders request making that modification permanent by amending §484.55(a)(2) and §484.55(b)(2) to allow PTs, SLPs, and OTs to conduct initial and comprehensive assessments whenever therapy services are ordered; rationale: increases flexibility, aligns with statutory permissions, supports access to care.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eliminate or extend 96-hour average length of stay CoP and remove 96-hour physician certification CoP for CAHs
rubrics_metrics.description: Eliminate or extend the 96-hour average length of stay condition of participation (CoPs) and remove the 96-hour physician certification CoP for critical access hospitals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rural hospitals report the annual length-of-stay and certification requirements are prohibitive; flexibility would permit treating patients locally as clinically appropriate and responding to system fluctuations (e.g., infectious surges, post-acute placement delays).

rubrics_metrics.name: Allow direct admission to rural hospital swing beds for Medicare patients meeting SNF requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Allow direct admission to rural hospital swing beds for Medicare patients who do not require acute care but do meet skilled nursing facility requirements at 42 C.F.R. §409.31.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Direct swing-bed admission can prevent deterioration that leads to costly inpatient admissions, save providers/HHS/beneficiaries money, and support access to quality care in rural communities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remove 3-day inpatient hospital stay requirement prior to Medicare SNF coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: Remove the 3-day rural hospital stay provision at 42 C.F.R §409.30 prior to Medicare coverage of a skilled nursing facility stay.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Originally enacted in 1965, the 3-day rule delays transfer to appropriate post-acute care; eliminating it would free up strained rural hospital capacity and let beneficiaries transfer sooner, improving access and resource use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extend site-neutral payment policy exemption to Medicare-Dependent Hospitals (MDHs)
rubrics_metrics.description: Extend the current site neutral payment policy exemption to Medicare-Dependent Hospitals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Site-neutral payment policies apply to off-campus HOPDs established after the Bipartisan Budget Act of 2015; Rural Sole Community Hospitals are exempt. Stakeholders request MDHs receive the same exemption because MDHs often serve as sole access points and may face higher volumes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eliminate mandatory CMMI model participation
rubrics_metrics.description: Eliminate mandatory Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Innovation (CMMI) models (e.g., TEAM, IOTA, EPM).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stakeholders argue mandatory participation increases costs and exceeds CMS' testing mandate; they urge return to voluntary innovation laboratory models focused on affordability, quality, and accessibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eliminate Inpatient Rehabilitation Facilities (IRFs) Review Choice Demonstration (RCD)
rubrics_metrics.description: Eliminate Inpatient Rehabilitation Facilities (IRFs) Review Choice Determinations (RCD).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: RCD implemented 100% pre-payment review in certain states; stakeholders claim it is administratively burdensome, provides high approval rates (>85%), and fails to reduce burden or costs; expansion to more states would institutionalize unnecessary practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remove new maternity care hospital Conditions of Participation
rubrics_metrics.description: Remove the New Maternity Care Hospital Conditions of Participation (CoPs).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Small hospitals contend CoPs for labor/delivery/prenatal/post-partum are counterproductive because readmission measures show little variation across hospitals and the CoPs do not meaningfully distinguish performance; recommendation is elimination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eliminate reporting of excessively burdensome and duplicative hospital quality measures
rubrics_metrics.description: Eliminate or revise hospital quality reporting requirements (PRO-PMs, structural measures, hybrid measures, readmission measures) that are excessively burdensome and duplicative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stakeholders report high administrative/compliance costs, little variation between hospitals, and limited utility for distinguishing performance. They recommend more targeted approaches (e.g., focusing on preventable readmissions) and note hybrid measures impose heavy burdens (matching claims to EHR data).

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluate necessity of administrative provisions impacting physicians
rubrics_metrics.description: Systematically evaluate the necessity and impact of administrative provisions imposed on clinicians to determine which regulations can be eliminated or revised without compromising care, safety, or program integrity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Physicians report spending substantial hours on paperwork (3–15+ hours/week) and practices spend billions annually on quality reporting; stakeholders ask CMS to adopt a structured framework, include standardized cost/burden/quality-impact assessments in Regulatory Impact and RFA analyses, and make assumptions available for public comment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Simplify and realign MIPS and Quality Payment Program
rubrics_metrics.description: Revise the structure of the Merit-based Incentive Payment System (MIPS) to reduce siloed performance categories and complexity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stakeholders recommend prioritizing rigorous measures that state purpose and importance, focus on appropriate care, have strong clinical evidence, clear/accurate specifications, and are feasible/applicable in practice to reduce burden and improve care.

rubrics_metrics.name: Better align Medicare Advantage and traditional Medicare policies
rubrics_metrics.description: Align Medicare Advantage and Medicare policies to promote transparency and reduce administrative burden for clinicians.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS should collaborate with Medicare Advantage Organizations to streamline contracting and administrative processes required for clinician participation in MA plans.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revise Stark law regulations that prohibit physicians monetizing intellectual property
rubrics_metrics.description: Revise regulations enforcing the Stark law (Section 1877) that prohibit independent physicians from monetizing their intellectual property.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stakeholders argue current CMS interpretations create barriers to physician entrepreneurship (royalties/licensing treated as remuneration), skew incentives toward private equity or institutions, and suggest regulatory revisions to permit physician benefit from IP without posing program integrity risks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eliminate 'Incident to Billing' (IB)
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Incident to Billing' (IB) should be eliminated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Nursing stakeholders say IB (APRN billed under physician NPI and reimbursed at 100% vs APRN at 85%) is anticompetitive, hinders new nursing businesses, and should be removed from 42 C.F.R. §410.26 to level the playing field.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standardize 'practitioner' terminology across federal regulations
rubrics_metrics.description: Standardize medical practitioner terms in regulations (use 'practitioner' for anyone who provides care across programs).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Different terms across programs cause confusion; CMS used 'practitioner' in final Physician Fee Schedule rule and stakeholders urge adoption government-wide so providers need not track program-specific terminology.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allow continued and expanded use of telehealth
rubrics_metrics.description: Encourage HHS to allow continued use of telehealth and rely on/improve 42 CFR §410.78(b) to permanently support telehealth services.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Telehealth expanded during the COVID-19 PHE and increased access; making flexibilities permanent where appropriate would reduce need for waivers and support rural access without congressional action for many services.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allow APRNs to practice at top of license / grant Full Practice Authority (FPA)
rubrics_metrics.description: HHS should allow advanced practice registered nurses (APRNs) to practice at the top of their license (Full Practice Authority) within federal programs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FPA permits APRNs to practice commensurate with education/training; stakeholders note many states still restrict FPA, pandemic flexibilities had no negative patient impacts, and federal action (e.g., VA National Standards) could allow APRNs to practice fully for patients covered by federal programs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eliminate outdated collaborative agreements and supervision requirements for APRNs
rubrics_metrics.description: Eliminate outdated regulations, onerous collaborative agreements, and unnecessary supervision requirements for APRNs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collaborative/supervision requirements were relaxed during COVID-19 without harming care; transition-to-practice agreements are increasingly hard to obtain and mergers complicate signing; stakeholders argue these requirements don't protect patients and hinder APRN practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reform CPT and RUC processes to better represent nonphysician perspectives
rubrics_metrics.description: CMS should reform the Current Procedural Terminology (CPT) and Relative Value Scale Update Committee (RUC) systems to better reflect nonphysician provider roles and include more nonphysician representation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reimbursement rates are determined via CPT/RUC (AMA-run); ANA argues nursing perspectives are underrepresented, creating bias toward physicians. Reform should increase nonphysician voices on panels to improve transparency and appropriate valuation of services provided by NPs, PAs, and other nonphysician clinicians.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibit non-nursing professional oversight/control of nursing practice
rubrics_metrics.description: Prohibit oversight and control of nursing practice by non-nursing professionals (e.g., physician membership on nursing boards).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stakeholders argue professions should self-regulate; requiring physician representation on nursing boards is unfair and creates malincentives. Recommendation: nursing licensure/regulation should be run by nurses without outside regulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Forbid non-compete agreements for nurses in Medicare/Medicaid facilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Forbid the use of non-compete agreements for nurses in Medicare and Medicaid facilities as anticompetitive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Nurses typically lack access to corporate secrets; non-competes restrict mobility, cap salaries, reduce employment opportunities, and may worsen nurse shortages. Alternatives like HIPAA non-disclosure agreements can protect patient/business information without limiting job mobility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reform Inflation Reduction Act Medicare Drug Price Negotiation Program (MDPNP) implementation / pharmacy reimbursements
rubrics_metrics.description: Reform the IRA's Medicare Drug Price Negotiation Program implementation so pharmacies are not financially harmed by MFP pricing and reimbursement timing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pharmacies currently float costs waiting for manufacturer reimbursements and risk underwater payments by PBMs. Stakeholders propose: (1) pay pharmacies at least MFP + commensurate dispensing fee for MFP drugs; (2) do not assess DIR fees on MFP drugs; (3) require manufacturers to effectuate MFP via the Medicare Transaction Facilitator Data/Payment Modules; (4) pay refunds equal to WAC minus MFP within 14 days; (5) require earlier submission of MFP effectuation plans to allow pharmacies to plan PBM/plan contracts. Rationale: avoid shortages, protect independent pharmacies' cash flow.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eliminate Medicare Transaction Facilitator enrollment requirement for network pharmacy agreements
rubrics_metrics.description: Eliminate the requirement (42 CFR §423.505(q)) that Part D sponsors' network contracts require pharmacies to be enrolled in the MDPNP's Medicare Transaction Facilitator Data Module.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stakeholders assert CMS lacks statutory authority to mandate Part D participation be tied to MDPNP participation; mandatory contractual enrollment in the MTF DM via PBM/plan contracts should be struck.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rescind increased lab director qualifications (42 CFR §493.1405(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: Rescind or revise changes increasing laboratory director educational/clinical laboratory training requirements in 42 CFR §493.1405(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Final rule raised emphasis on 'clinical laboratory training' and two years' supervisory experience for high complexity testing, potentially reducing number of MDs qualifying as lab directors, risking laboratory closures and reduced access (esp. rural). Stakeholders urge reverting to prior standards to avoid workforce shortages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restore nursing degree eligibility for technical consultant qualification (42 CFR §493.1411(b)(4)(i)(A))
rubrics_metrics.description: Restore the nursing degree as a qualifying degree to operate as a technical consultant for moderately complex POC testing (42 CFR §493.1411(b)(4)(i)(A)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The final rule removed nursing degrees from eligible degrees, reducing nurses' ability to serve as technical consultants. No issues were identified previously with nurses in these roles; removing them will overburden labs and impede timely results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rescind heightened blood gas testing personnel qualification (42 CFR §493.1423(b)(7))
rubrics_metrics.description: Rescind the change imposing higher educational requirements for blood gas analysis testing personnel under 42 CFR §493.1423(b)(7).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The final rule's heightened requirement conflicts with CLIA preamble and excludes EMTs (who often have high school diplomas plus training) from running blood gases on POC devices; this undermines critical care during transport and emergency settings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rescind alternative sanctions for Certificate of Waiver (CoW) labs (42 CFR §493.1804(c)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: Rescind provisions allowing imposition of alternative (financial) sanctions against CoW laboratories for improper proficiency testing referrals (42 CFR §493.1804(c)(1)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Alternative sanctions are unnecessary and unfair for waived labs; proficiency testing is not required for waived testing, and sanctioning ~200,000 CoW labs is impractical, increases compliance costs, risks reducing patient access, and diverts accrediting organizations' resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revise/Rescind other CLIA Subpart F general administration changes
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommend rescinding or revising additional CLIA Subpart F (General Administration) changes in the 2023 CLIA final rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Medical device/lab stakeholders express concern that several administrative and personnel-related changes in the CLIA final rule will exacerbate workforce shortages, increase closures, and negatively affect patient care and access; they request CMS reconsider those administrative provisions.
